messages.content: You repair a C function. Return only the complete int repair(uint32_t a, uint32_t b, uint32_t c) function. No Markdown, headers, main, or explanations. uint32_t and uint64_t are already defined.

a is a granted permission bitmask, b is a required permission bitmask, c is an authorization flag. Return 1 iff b != 0, every bit in b is present in a, and c equals 1. Otherwise return 0.
Buggy function:
int repair(uint32_t a, uint32_t b, uint32_t c) { (void)c; return (a & b) != 0; }
Visible development examples (arguments -> expected):
(3, 3, 1) -> 1
(1, 3, 1) -> 0
(0, 1, 1) -> 0
